answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our economy enforces quadratic stake burning for registering concurrent identity slots. An agent cannot harbor fraudulent clones because creating n identities mandates burning stake proportional to n^2 tokens into an unrecoverable ember pool. This superlinear cost scaling provides an economic barrier: while legitimate actors pay negligible fees, attackers face compounding losses that quickly shred any velvet illusion of low-overhead automation.
